item.title: FBI blames North Korea for $6.3 billion Binance crypto hack
item.description: According to the CISA, TraderTraitor is a North Korean state-sponsored hacking group that has been associated with cryptocurrency thefts and cyberattack tactics since at least 2020.

item.title: The world according to Ellen von Unwerth: Glamour, sensuality and photography
item.description: Euronews Culture sat down with the renowned German photographer Ellen von Unwerth to discuss her contribution to Maurizio Cattelan and Pierpaolo Ferrari's 2027 Toiletpaper calendar, her unique approach to fashion photography and the stories behind some of her most iconic images.

item.title: Russia says 'massive' drone attack targeted 'industrial enterprise' amid reports oil refinery hit
item.description: Telegram war monitoring channels said an attack had targeted the Kstovo oil refinery - also known as the Lukoil-Nizhegorodnefteorgsintez refinery, thought to be one of Russia's largest such facilities.

item.title: Hooray for Houdini: Budapest celebrates 100th anniversary of escape artist's death
item.description: An event honouring the greatest escape artist and most influential magician of all time has brought Harry Houdini's only living descendant, his brother's grandchild, to Budapest. The centenary for the former "King of Shackles" is also being celebrated by a film festival and an artwork.

item.title: EU Commission: Polish Parliament has right to appoint judges to the Constitutional Court
item.description: The statement comes after a confrontation outside the Constitutional Tribunal building on Friday night, broadcast live on television, that has pushed a decade-old dispute into the wider European political debate.

item.title: Europe’s crumbling coastlines face a €800 billion crisis. Is it time to move inland?
item.description: Economic losses from coastal erosion exceed €1 billion per year across 28 European countries

item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 1st, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Doha stopover travel guide: What to see and do on a city break in Qatar's capital
item.description: Qatar’s capital Doha offers plenty for travellers on a stopover, whether it’s a 24-hour stay or a few days. Here’s what to see, where to dine and what to experience beyond the airport.

item.title: Poland crisis: Donald Tusk strikes defiant tone vowing ‘no compromise’ on rule of law after Tribunal clash
item.description: Tusk addressed the nation as tensions over Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal escalated, accusing PiS and President Nawrocki of undermining the rule of law and pledging support for the newly elected judges and the court’s work.

item.title: Abu Dhabi Grand Slam 2026: Heavyweights deliver a spectacular finale
item.description: The Abu Dhabi Grand Slam concluded with thrilling heavyweight action! Ivaylo Ivanov, Yelyzaveta Lytvynenko, Idar Bifov, Helena Vukovic and Irakli Demetrashvili claimed gold, while judo legend Teddy Riner joined the celebrations.

item.title: Berlin student protests: youth demands meet extremist mobilisation
item.description: According to police, around 5,000 people joined a demonstration by the initiative "Gen Z regelt" at Berlin’s Brandenburg Gate. In the afternoon, organisers claimed some 11,000 participants had taken part.

item.title: France's third weekend of social protests sees lower turnout and early clashes in major cities
item.description: According to the Interior Ministry, the authorised marches proceeded peacefully. But tensions rose during their dispersal in Paris, Lyon, Marseille and other major cities.

item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 31st, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Spain observes third day of mourning as unions demand urgent action following deadly train collision
item.description: Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez is facing mounting pressure following the incident, which has further knocked confidence in Spain’s rail infrastructure.

item.title: 'A lot of lies': Kaja Kallas criticises Russian FM Lavrov following G20 meetings
item.description: British Foreign Minister Ed Miliband said he had told Lavrov in the plenary that "he should have the courage to tell Putin that Russia will not win this war."

item.title: 'Northern women and esotericism': Life after death explored at Finnish National Gallery
item.description: The relationship between spirit and matter, questions related to life after death and the existence of the spirit world are the key themes of the exhibition "Arcana Borealis – Northern Women and Esotericism" at Ateneum Art Museum, Finnish National Gallery.

item.title: Evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky arrive in Ukraine amid localised truce between Kyiv and Moscow
item.description: It comes as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said around 280,000 Ukrainian households had been left without power after Russian strikes overnight.

item.title: Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal crisis explained: a decade-long dispute over legitimacy of the justice
item.description: The dispute over Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal began in 2015, when the two main political camps, PO and PiS, clashed over the appointment of five judges. It later escalated into a wider conflict over judicial independence, the Tribunal’s composition and the authority of its rulings.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 31st, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 31st, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Poland political crisis: Constitutional court in chaos as Nawrocki accuses government of staging power grab
item.description: Riot police were deployed outside Poland's Constitutional Tribunal on Friday after its president was suspended, escalating a power struggle over the court.

item.title: Kärcher boss: Less regulation, more action to get Europe and Germany fit again
item.description: Kärcher, best known for its pressure washers, recorded €3.5 billion in sales in 2025 and employs 17,000 people worldwide. Its CEO warns of a 'perfect storm' and calls for a fitness plan for Germany and Europe.

item.title: The seven days I thought I might have breast cancer
item.description: Seven days of uncertainty following a breast biopsy become a deeply personal reckoning with cancer, family history and fear. From that experience, Euronews reporter Monica Pinna explores Europe's persistent inequalities in early detection and care.

item.title: Zelenskyy thanks US over deal for 500 Patriot missiles but warns delivery could take years
item.description: Kyiv has long called for more interceptors to help its forces fend off Russian missile and drone attacks. The rapidly approaching winter is pressing home that need.

item.title: Syrian curriculum changes spark debate over removal of images and historical figures
item.description: Changes were not limited to the texts; images and illustrations were also edited in Photoshop, adding hijabs or long robes to female figures, deleting women's photos, and covering or replacing statues, sculptures and artworks.

item.title: Travelling beyond the borders of Baku through fiction
item.description: What connects an Iranian novelist exploring women's lives, a British children's author creating imaginary worlds and an Azerbaijani writer preserving her country's cultural identity? The answer is stories that cross borders, connect continents, and blend cultures through books.

item.title: Curfews, 70,000 police and Halloween fears: France braces for fresh protests
item.description: Mass protests are expected to sweep across France this Saturday, coinciding with Halloween celebrations as authorities deploy a major security operation.

item.title: France aims for 'responsible' 2027 budget as Fitch downgrades outlook
item.description: The US rating agency doubts France's ability to sustainably restore its public finances after the 2027 presidential election, probably followed by parliamentary elections. The government, for its part, reiterates the "absolute necessity" of having a budget adopted by the end of the year.

item.title: How many bats are killed by wind turbines? Study warns of ‘shocking’ increase amid clean energy boom
item.description: Researchers warn the death toll of bats has spiralled since the boom in wind energy – but there are solutions at hand.

item.title: 11 ‘extraordinary’ European hotels included on Fodor's Finest list for 2027
item.description: A new list of the 50 most incredible hotels in the world features 11 properties in Europe.

item.title: Where in Europe do people spend over 40% of their income on housing?
item.description: Housing costs take up more than 40% of disposable income for millions of Europeans. Euronews Business takes a closer look at which countries are hit hardest, with experts explaining the drivers.

item.title: Polish president cuts short trip to Senegal amid court 'coup d'état' claims
item.description: The Polish government has been pushing to remove the Constitutional Tribunal's judges, who were appointed by the previous right-wing administration led by the nationalist Law and Justice (PiS) party.

item.title: Abu Dhabi Grand Slam 2026: Middleweights Shine on Day 2
item.description: Day 2 of the Abu Dhabi Grand Slam delivered thrilling judo! Angelika Szymanska, Hassan Doukkali, Tais Pina and Petru Pelivan claimed gold, with historic first Grand Slam titles for Morocco and Moldova.

item.title: Brazil claims it questioned Argentina over Bolsonaro's escape, Buenos Aires denies it
item.description: According to Argentina's migration authorities, Bolsonaro boarded a private plane in the northeastern city of Puerto Iguazú on Tuesday evening, just 40 minutes after crossing into the country by land.

item.title: Canada aims to become EU's first 'associate member' by June 2027, Carney says
item.description: Mark Carney has set June 2027 as the deadline to make Canada the European Union's first-ever "associate member". The category, which has no precedent, has been fiercely opposed by Germany.

item.title: French economy 'at a standstill' as budget uncertainty swirls
item.description: France has recorded no growth since the start of the year, while GDP fell 0.1% between July and September. The government is urging political forces to adopt the 2027 budget, as the country's ability to reassure markets is in doubt.

item.title: UN envoy pushes for renewed Cyprus talks before end of 2026
item.description: Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhürman said in Ankara that "we will continue to work for a fair and sustainable solution on the island, in close consultation and cooperation with Turkey."

item.title: EU diplomats object to G20 photo with Lavrov, prompting US cancellation
item.description: The meeting in Atlanta will go ahead as planned, ahead of a G20 leaders’ summit hosted by President Donald Trump at his Miami golf club in December.

item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 30th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Turkic states press on with Asia-Europe transport projects as new opportunities emerge
item.description: The Ankara Declaration highlighted the trade and transport cooperation of the Turkish states. Uzbekistan proposed 100 industrial projects spanning critical minerals and green technology, while Turkey signed new agreements with Uzbekistan and reaffirmed a $15bn (€13.5bn) trade goal with Kazakhstan.

item.title: Residents leave Russian-occupied Oleshky amid local ceasefire
item.description: The White House said US first lady Melania Trump helped negotiate the ceasefire and coordinate the humanitarian mission.

item.title: EU to fast-track €45 billion for Ukraine amid acute financial crunch
item.description: In 2027, the EU will provide Ukraine with €32 billion in military aid and €13 billion in budget support. But more funds will be needed as Russia escalates.

item.title: Protesters clash with police near Colosseum as Italy stages nationwide strike
item.description: People have taken to the streets again in dozens of Italian cities to protest against the rising cost of living, as part of a general strike called by grassroots unions.

item.title: Pakistan: Islamabad zoo introduces 'Coffee with Alpaca' attraction
item.description: Coffee with a side of alpacas? At a zoo near Islamabad, visitors can enjoy drinks and snacks while watching, feeding and petting the animals. The attraction features ten imported alpacas, a first for Pakistan according to the zoo.

item.title: Manosphere's impact on boys and men calls for public health action, report warns
item.description: The ‘manosphere’ is fuelling harmful attitudes and worsening health inequalities among boys and men, prompting calls for a public health response that addresses the root causes of its growing appeal.

item.title: Russian independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta says it will shut down following pressure from Kremlin
item.description: The paper is one of the few Russian outlets that has been openly critical of Russia's war in Ukraine, but it has come under increasing pressure from Moscow.

item.title: Iran’s Revolutionary Guard reports three tankers on fire in Strait of Hormuz as talks continue
item.description: Iran’s Revolutionary Guard said Friday that two oil tankers had caught fire and been stopped in the Strait of Hormuz, as Qatari mediators returned to Tehran for another round of talks aimed at ending the war between Iran and the United States.

item.title: UK probes Meta over 'exploitative' new terms for media as global pushback mounts
item.description: Britain's competition watchdog has opened an investigation into whether Meta was imposing "exploitative" new terms allowing it to use media content for its own products, including AI, without giving publishers adequate choice.

item.title: EU to impose €2 fee on all packages entering the bloc as of 1 November
item.description: A €3 fee also came into force in July, leading to a 60% drop in small parcel imports over three months. The new rules aim to counter imports from Chinese platforms, whose low prices threaten European retailers.

item.title: PSG to defend Intercontinental Cup title in December as Qatar hosts final stage
item.description: Continental champions will compete in Qatar this December as PSG seek a second successive Intercontinental Cup title. The final stages return for a third year, following earlier matches in Saudi Arabia and South Africa.
